first_impression.reaction: Googled 'oceania wedding destinations' on the train. I wanted a list. The first line sort of gives me one, and it's dated November 2026, which is good. But the Key Takeaways say 'ten places' without naming them, and one bullet is just about which ones have a guide on their site. The table with all ten is the thing I actually wanted, and it's right at the bottom. I'd skim one or two islands, find the table, screenshot it, bookmark the page. I wouldn't enquire.

journey.quote: Oceania wedding destinations run from the islands of Melanesia and Polynesia to New Zealand, Hawaii and Australia's own reef islands.
journey.reaction: Okay, the heading matches what I typed and I get the rough area in one line. Good start.

journey.quote: Ten places, unranked, run from Fiji to Tahiti in four groups: Melanesia, Polynesia, New Zealand and the Whitsundays.
journey.reaction: Which ten though? Just tell me the names. I don't know if Vanuatu or Samoa is in Melanesia or Polynesia, so the group names don't help me.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller dates Fiji's cyclone season from November to April, so a covered ceremony space and a buffer day belong in the plan for much of the tropical South Pacific.
journey.reaction: This one's useful. It's dated and it tells me what to do about it. I'd screenshot it.

journey.quote: Fiji, Hawaii, New Zealand and the Whitsundays each have a full guide of ours, and the six other places are covered on this page alone.
journey.reaction: Why is this a key takeaway? It's about their website, not my wedding. I'd rather have seen a pointer to the table.

journey.section: How we chose these Oceania destinations
journey.quote: The stations differ in period and in what counts as a rain day: Nadi covers 1961 to 1990, Apia 1971 to 2000 and Hamilton Island 2002 to 2026, so read each figure on its own terms.
journey.reaction: Too much methodology for me on a phone. I believe you that it's sourced. Scrolled past.

journey.quote: shows January to March as the wettest months, with March at 324.0 mm, and July the driest at 46.0 mm.
journey.reaction: Wettest and driest months in plain words. That's the kind of answer I want for every island.

journey.quote: March brings 330.4 mm over 21 rain days, and September 87.2 mm over 11.
journey.reaction: I don't know what 87 mm means. Is September a good month or not? Just say it.

journey.quote: Curfews and alcohol bans can come at short notice, flights may be suspended with little or no warning, and demonstrations may increase around 13 May, 24 September and elections.
journey.reaction: Honestly glad they said this. Most 'top destinations' lists would just show a lagoon photo. Makes me trust the rest more.

journey.quote: Since 5 November, aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats have been barred from Santo International Airport until its rescue and firefighting services are fully running.
journey.reaction: 5 November of which year? Is this still true when I read it?

journey.quote: Expect a request for a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or Certificat de Célibat and a Certificat de Coutume, and possibly apostilles on Australian documents.
journey.reaction: Lots of French paperwork, and it's all about Australian documents. I'm in Singapore, so I'm not sure any of this applies to me. Skimmed it.

journey.quote: For November 2025 only, [Earth Sciences New Zealand's summary of that month](https://niwa.co.nz/climate-and-weather/monthly/climate-summary-november-2025) records a nationwide 15.9°C, a new November record and 2.2°C warmer than the 1991 to 2020 normal.
journey.reaction: Under 'When to go' I get one month from last year? That doesn't tell me when to go. Felt like the answer was missing.

journey.quote: Closer to home, the reef islands offer warm water and Australian law, with no passport needed.
journey.reaction: Not closer to my home. It's very clearly written for Australians.

journey.section: Oceania wedding destinations at a glance
journey.quote: | Destination | Region | Wet or cyclone season (as the source states it) | Getting married | Our guide |
journey.reaction: THIS is what I came for. All ten, season and legal route side by side. Screenshot. But I had to scroll past nine sections to find it on my phone.

journey.quote: Hawaii sits in Polynesia, so it belongs here, but it is a US state north of the equator, with a wetter winter from October to April.
journey.reaction: I literally wondered this when I saw Hawaii in the intro. Short, direct, good FAQ.

journey.section: Plan your Oceania wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Advisor quotes in AUD, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD, so Australian company. And there's no idea of what anything costs anywhere on the page. Fine for later, not for me now.

unanswered_questions: Roughly how much does a wedding cost in each of these places, or which ones are cheaper? Nothing on the page gives any sense of cost.
When is the best month to go for New Zealand, Tonga and the Cook Islands? Those sections give a cyclone season or one past month, not a best-month answer.
Is September a good month in Vanuatu? The page gives mm figures but doesn't say plainly.
Which year is the Santo airport restriction from, and is it still in place?
Does the legal advice change if we aren't Australian (for example living in Singapore)? Most of the legal lines are framed around Australian documents.
Which of these are easiest to fly to for guests? Nothing on flight times or connections.
How does Wedded Wonderland's fee work, and do you plan for couples who don't live in Australia? (deferred business detail)
Can I see a real wedding you've planned in any of these places? (deferred business detail)
